bio: Melvin McNair was a Vietnam veteran who became involved in Black-liberation and antiwar politics after experiencing racism during his military service. On July 31, 1972 he along with his wife Jean and three other companions, hijacked Delta Air Lines Flight 841 out of Detroit, demanding ransom and passage to Algeria to join the Black Panther International Section. The hijackers released all 86 passengers in Miami before flying on to Algiers. Disillusioned with exile in Algeria, the group moved to France, where they were arrested in 1976 and tried for the hijacking. After his release from prison McNair settled in Caen, Normandy, where he worked at an orphanage and coached youth baseball until his retirement.
